chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Muyassir, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I instruct the slave-girl, and she washes my garment from semen, but she does not thoroughly wash it, and I pray in it, then it turns out that it is dry.
He عليه السلام said: “Repeat your salat. Indeed, had you washed it yourself, there would have been nothing upon you.”

key_terms.أَعِدْ: repeat, referring to repeating the salat
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةَ: the slave-girl instructed to wash the garment
key_terms.ثَوْبِي: my garment in which salat was performed
key_terms.صَلَاتَكَ: your salat that must be repeated
key_terms.يَابِسٌ: dry, meaning the garment was found dried after washing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone prays in a garment inadequately washed from semen?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying in a garment that was not properly cleansed of semen. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام instructs that the salat must be repeated when inadequate washing is discovered, and indicates that if the person had washed it himself, no liability would have remained upon him.
